title: Question 7
stem: A stationary nucleus X decays by emitting a β⁺ particle to form a nucleus of carbon-13 (¹³₆C). An incomplete equation to represent this decay is X → ¹³₆C + β⁺.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the name of the class (group) of particles that includes $β^{+}$.
hints: Hint 1: Consider the physical mechanism underlying this process based on fundamental particles and quarks.
walkthrough:

Step 2: **Analyze the Physical Mechanism**
Apply the criteria to the given physical setup: lepton(s).

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The carbon-13 nucleus has a mass of $2.2 \times 10^{-26}\,\mathrm{kg}$. Its kinetic energy as a result of the decay process is 0.80 MeV.
Calculate the speed of this nucleus.
speed = $m s ^{1} $
hints: Hint 1: Identify the given data from the problem and recall the governing equation connecting these quantities using kinetic energy.
Hint 2: Rearrange the formula to isolate the required quantity before substituting numerical values with correct powers of ten.
Hint 3: Check your intermediate calculation steps carefully and ensure your final answer is stated to an appropriate number of significant figures with correct SI units.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
Identify the core physical principle governing this problem: Kinetic energy. State the relevant formula or theoretical relationship clearly.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Substitute the known quantities into the formula with correct SI units and powers of ten:
$$E = ½mv2; = 0.80 × 106 × 1.60 × 10-19; = 1.28 × 10-13 (J) v2 = 2 × 1.28 × 10-13 / 2.2 × 10-26 v = 3.4 × 106 m s-1$$
Work through the intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
